tasks.short: Check and approve payment requests before the bank batch goes out.

today.trigger: A bookkeeper or a site submits a payment request, or an agency invoice is ready to pay.
steps: Open the request in AFAS Profit and find the invoice, the purchase order and the contract on SharePoint.
Check the cost-centre budget, the signatory mandate and whether the same invoice was paid before.
Compare the supplier IBAN with the last payment to that supplier.
Approve, refuse, or send the request back for a missing document.
The bookkeeper puts the approved items into a Rabobank SEPA batch.
drudgery: Repeating the budget, duplicate and IBAN checks on requests that sit inside the rules
Chasing invoice copies and contract versions by email
Comparing IBANs against old payment lists
today.time_sinks: The queue of routine requests, plus the back-and-forth when a document is missing. Peak months add a wave of invoices from the three staffing agencies.

lenses.faster: The budget, contract, duplicate and IBAN checks leave the controller's desk. What stays is the exception queue and the batch approval, about an hour a week in a normal month and longer when the agency invoices peak.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when an AFAS payment proposal is created or an agency invoice is imported. The four checks run on their own and a clean batch is assembled inside the mandate. The gate is the controller's release: a failed check or an amount above the mandate cannot go in that batch.
lenses.ambitious: The decision of whether a flex order at Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo fits that site's labour budget moves to the morning the order is placed, instead of waiting for the agency invoice weeks later. Demand would grow in the peak, because site managers would ask for that check on the large orders they now place without one.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing copies and redoing the same four checks. The controller keeps the few payments that move the cash forecast, such as a disputed agency rate or a new warehouse lease.
lenses.options: Two payment dates for the same approved batch, pay on term or pay the agency early where the contract gives a discount, change whether the Rabobank balance still covers wage tax, VAT and payroll. The controller releases one date and holds the other.
lenses.altitude: The week starts with an exception queue instead of a pile of requests. The controller gains the right to send a batch back when a rule fails, and to refuse an IBAN change that has no second approver, while the Finance Director still signs above the higher mandate. The job becomes more expert on fraud patterns and agency rates, and less of a signature step.
reach: The accountant's split of annual invoices for rent, insurance and fuel cards into the right months, once the controller learns the accrual keys already used in AFAS Profit.

tasks.human_edge: The controller still has to judge a real dispute: a rate that does not match the agency contract, a new supplier, or a lease that the budget did not expect. Rules cannot tell a wrong IBAN from a genuine bank change, and a person who can change a supplier IBAN must not be the person who sends the batch.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget left, an open order or contract, a duplicate invoice number or amount, and an IBAN that differs from the last payment are rules. AFAS and the Rabobank batch can apply them without a model. A person still releases the money.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS payment proposal is created, or an agency invoice is imported from a staffing portal.
steps: Rules compare the invoice with the open order or contract, the cost-centre budget, earlier invoices with the same number or amount, and the IBAN on the last paid invoice.
Requests that pass and sit inside the controller's mandate are collected into one SEPA batch.
A failed rule, a changed IBAN, or an amount above the mandate goes to an exception queue with the failed rule named.
The controller approves or returns each exception. Amounts above the Finance Director's mandate wait for that second approval.
A second authorised user, who cannot change a supplier IBAN, sends the approved batch to Rabobank.
in_practice.human_gate: No batch is sent until the controller approves it, and a failed check cannot be released in bulk. The person who changes a supplier IBAN is not the person who sends the batch.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS workflow history and a SharePoint control folder, with the rule version, the checks that ran, and the approver's name and time.

evidence.claim: A payment request can be tested against budget, an open contract or order, a duplicate invoice and a changed IBAN with rules written down, and left for a person above the mandate.
AFAS bank matching, the closest shipped control on this ledger, applies fixed rules on reference, IBAN and invoice number rather than a model.

risks: A changed IBAN on a real agency invoice is the fraud this control is for. It fails if one person can change the supplier master and also send the batch.
Agency hours can match a rate card and still be wrong. The rule will pass a plausible invoice.
If most spend has no purchase order, the exception queue becomes the whole queue and the time saving disappears.
Payment references can name an employee, for example on an attachment of earnings. Those references should stay out of a wide SharePoint group.
Coding the mandate wrong, or leaving a leaver as an approver, authorises payments the Finance Director never intended.
research_questions: What share of AFAS payment requests last quarter were inside the mandate, matched an order or contract, and used an unchanged IBAN?
Who can change a supplier or agency IBAN today, and who else must approve that change?
What share of agency invoices have no purchase order or rate card in AFAS, only a portal PDF?
How many duplicate or wrong-IBAN payments occurred in the last year, and what did they cost?

tasks.short: Watch the cash and the dates for tax, pension and payroll.

today.trigger: Each morning, and again before a payment run or a wage-tax, VAT or pension due date.
steps: Download the Rabobank statement and check that it landed in the AFAS bank journal.
Build the cash position in Excel from the bank, open receivables, open payables and the payroll calendar.
Clear the bank lines AFAS did not match.
Compare the balance with the reserve the Finance Director expects and with the statutory due dates.
Tell the Finance Director if a payment run should wait.
drudgery: Copying statement lines into the cash workbook
Rebuilding the same 15-day calendar of wage tax, VAT, pension and payroll
Hunting unmatched lines that already carry an invoice number
today.time_sinks: The workbook itself, and the unmatched remainder after AFAS has applied its match on reference, IBAN and invoice number. The nightly Power BI extract is often already stale for this decision.

lenses.faster: Building the cash workbook from the statement and the open items disappears. The morning review of unmatched lines, the reserve test and any hold takes about twenty minutes on a quiet day.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the Rabobank CAMT.053 file lands in AFAS. The match, the position, the reserve test and the 15-day calendar of wage tax, VAT, pension and industry-fund dates run on their own. The gate is a hold on any payment run that would break the reserve or a statutory date.
lenses.ambitious: The credit and collections officer and the three site managers get a morning figure for cash left after wage tax, VAT, pension and the next payroll, so a tight week is visible before a flex order is confirmed. Demand would grow when agency invoices cluster, because those people do not ask today while the workbook is still being built.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying CAMT lines into Excel. The controller keeps the morning when the gap is real: delay this agency batch, or call the Finance Director about the Rabobank facility.
lenses.options: Three reserve floors, statutory payments only, statutory payments plus two weeks of agency labour, or those two plus a capex hold, change whether Friday's SEPA run is released. The Finance Director's choice of floor is the decision.
lenses.altitude: Mornings start from a prepared position. The controller gains the right to hold a run that would break the agreed reserve, and to require a same-day note to the Finance Director when a statutory date is at risk. The job becomes more expert on liquidity and less on spreadsheet assembly.
reach: The bookkeeper's classification of bank lines the AFAS rules cannot match, once the controller learns the CAMT.053 references Rabobank sends and the AFAS bank-match screen.

tasks.human_edge: The controller is the one who can tell a timing gap, a customer who pays on Monday, from a structural one, a weak week in Venlo. The same person decides whether a statutory payment is ever allowed to wait. The machine can show the gap and must not move the reserve floor.
tasks.pattern_why: The position, the AFAS match on reference, IBAN and invoice number, and the due-date test are rules. A model is not required for the reserve test. The unmatched remainder can stay a list for a person.

in_practice.trigger: Rabobank delivers the CAMT.053 file and AFAS imports it.
steps: AFAS matching rules clear lines that agree on reference, IBAN and invoice number.
A script builds today's available cash from the bank balance, open receivables, open payables and the payroll journal.
It tests that balance against the reserve floor and against wage-tax, VAT, pension and industry-fund due dates for the next 15 days.
Unmatched lines and any breach are listed for the morning. The nightly Power BI extract is not the source of this balance.
The controller acknowledges a clean day, or holds or releases the payment run when the floor or a due date is threatened.
in_practice.human_gate: A run that would break the reserve floor or pay a statutory amount late waits for the controller. The floor is changed only by the controller together with the Finance Director.
data_needed: Payroll, wage-tax, VAT and pension calendar
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank journal and a SharePoint treasury log that records the reserve floor in force, the test result, and any hold, with the time and the person.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank statement lines with fixed rules on reference, IBAN and invoice number.
With SEPA batches and CAMT.053 files, cheque deposits are negligible for a Dutch company of this kind, so the cash position can be built from the bank file and the ledger.
A documented close control is that nothing posts until bank, accounts receivable and accounts payable tie to zero. The same three ties are what make a morning cash figure reliable.

risks: The nightly Power BI extract is too stale to authorise a same-day payment run. Using it as the balance would recreate the spreadsheet risk.
A reserve floor that ignores the peak, when flex goes toward 300 people, will either cry wolf in quiet months or miss the Q4 cash squeeze.
Unmatched lines treated as explained cash will overstate what is available.
Bank text can name employees on expense claims or attachments of earnings. The treasury log should keep those lines out of a broad folder.
If Rabobank only delivers a PDF in practice, the deterministic import does not get off the ground.
research_questions: How many hours stale is the Power BI finance extract versus the Rabobank balance on a normal morning?
What share of bank lines did AFAS match last month on reference, IBAN and invoice number, and how long did the remainder take?
Is there a written reserve floor or a Rabobank covenant today, and who may change it?
Which wage-tax, VAT, pension or industry-fund payments were late in the last year?

tasks.short: Decide whether we should draw on the bank or place a surplus.

today.trigger: The current account looks high or low, a facility review is due, or the forecast shows a gap before payroll or VAT.
steps: Take the 13-week cash view from the FP&A analysts, or build it from AFAS open items.
Set payroll, wage tax, VAT, pension, agency invoices and known capex against the Rabobank limit.
Try one or two placements or draws on paper.
Write a recommendation to the Finance Director.
After approval, the person with the bank mandate calls Rabobank or sends the instruction.
drudgery: Rebuilding the cash waterfall before the conversation can start
Collecting due dates from payroll and tax that belong on one calendar
Retyping facility headroom from the last Rabobank letter
today.time_sinks: Assembly of the view, especially in peak weeks when agency invoices move the apparent surplus from one week to the next.

lenses.faster: Assembling the waterfall and the statutory due dates disappears. Writing the recommendation and agreeing it with the Finance Director still takes about half a day in a week when money moves, and less when the advice is to do nothing.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the weekly treasury log shows a surplus above the reserve floor or a gap against the next statutory dates. The copilot drafts the placements or the draw. The gate is the Finance Director's approval before anyone instructs Rabobank.
lenses.ambitious: The place-or-draw decision is taken every week of the peak, instead of only when the balance looks extreme at month end. Demand would grow in the weeks the balance swings, because the Finance Director would use a note that is already prepared and today asks only when the account looks out of line.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the same waterfall in Excel. The controller keeps the argument about how much of the surplus is real once the unbilled agency hours are counted.
lenses.options: Three uses of the same surplus, leave it on the current account, place it for one month at Rabobank, or pay an agency early for a contractual discount, produce different balances on the wage-tax and payroll dates inside that month. The Finance Director picks one, and the other two are real rejected decisions.
lenses.altitude: The week has a short funding meeting instead of a spreadsheet build. The controller gains the right to table a recommended draw or deposit, with the cash effect on statutory dates shown. The Finance Director keeps the right to place or draw the money. The work becomes more expert on liquidity and less on file gathering.
reach: The FP&A analyst's maintenance of the 13-week cash model, once the controller learns the agency-hour, tariff and customer-collection drivers behind it.

tasks.human_edge: How much cash to keep back for a customer who pays late, a bad week at the port, or a flex spike is a judgement the Finance Director makes with the controller. The copilot cannot instruct Rabobank, and cash allocation stays with the person who holds the mandate.
tasks.pattern_why: The alternatives can be drafted from the treasury policy and the cash calendar, but the choice depends on counterparties, the facility and a relationship with Rabobank. The steps are predictable, so an agent is unnecessary. The person remains the lead and signs the allocation.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly treasury log shows cash above the reserve floor, or a gap before wage tax, VAT, pension or payroll.
steps: The position and the statutory calendar are taken from the treasury log rather than rebuilt.
The copilot drafts two or three uses of a surplus, or two ways to cover a gap, inside the written treasury policy on counterparties and maximum term.
Each draft shows the balance on the wage-tax, VAT, pension and payroll dates that fall inside the term.
The controller edits the recommendation and sits with the Finance Director.
The person named on the Rabobank mandate places the deposit or draws the facility, and files the bank confirmation.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves every placement and every draw before anyone contacts Rabobank. The controller does not move the money.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint treasury folder with the recommendation, the source figures, the Finance Director's approval and the bank confirmation. Not a personal model account.

evidence.claim: Tax estimates and cash allocation need mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.
An estimate the auditor cannot rebuild, because the prompt and the output sit in a personal account, is a documented failure mode for finance work that uses a model.
No product in the reviewed set places surplus cash or draws a Rabobank facility on an AFAS ledger. The draft has to be built for this company and then approved by a person.

risks: A draft that maximises interest can put the wage-tax or pension date inside a deposit term. The calendar check is the control that stops that.
A surplus that is only unbilled agency cost will be placed and then has to be broken when the invoices arrive.
If the facility covenant limits cash leaving the Rabobank group, a deposit draft that ignores it is unusable.
A recommendation stored only in a personal model account cannot be rebuilt by the Finance Director or the auditor.
research_questions: What is the Rabobank facility limit, rate and covenant, and who on the mandate may draw or place funds?
How many weeks a year does the current account hold more than one payroll plus the VAT payment?
Do the FP&A analysts already keep a 13-week cash forecast, and how far off was it in the last peak?
Is there a written treasury policy on counterparties, maximum term and the minimum that must stay on the current account?

tasks.short: Run the budget and the forecast across the three sites.

today.trigger: The budget calendar opens, a reforecast is called, or a site asks for spend the plan does not hold.
steps: Ask Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo and the FP&A analysts for their submissions.
Consolidate the workbooks, with own staff and agency labour often in different shapes.
Challenge the odd lines in meetings with the site managers.
Direct any funding consequence back to the treasury recommendation.
Take the pack to the Finance Director to lock.
drudgery: Chasing late site files and merging versions of the same workbook
Reformatting agency hours that arrive in three portal layouts
Retyping a cost-centre total that does not tie to AFAS
today.time_sinks: The consolidation week, and the repeat meetings caused by a file that does not tie to the ledger.

lenses.faster: Chasing and merging the three site files disappears. The challenge meetings and the lock with the Finance Director stay, and they still take the two or three meetings they take today.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the budget calendar opens or a site's volume move makes the flex line unbelievable. The pack and the challenge questions are drafted. The gate is the Finance Director locking the plan after the controller's challenge meeting.
lenses.ambitious: Each site manager gets a pack that shows agency hours on their own line against the CAO workforce, in time for the site planning meeting, instead of a company total after the lock. Demand would grow, because a site would ask for a fresh flex line whenever volume moves, and today a new pack means another consolidation week.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the version chase in Excel. The controller keeps the challenge meeting, where a site has to defend the flex assumption behind its cost.
lenses.options: Two frames for the same volume, more own staff on the CAO or more flex through the agencies, change hiring, the holiday-allowance accrual and whether the works council must be consulted. A third frame with lower volume at one site changes which cost centres are cut. The frame is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The month has a budget calendar and site reviews instead of a fortnight of merging files. The controller gains the right to send a site pack back when the flex line has no volume behind it. The Finance Director still locks the budget. The job becomes more expert as the person who challenges the plan, and less of a consolidator.
reach: The FP&A analyst's consolidation of the three site submissions into one pack, once the controller learns the driver file and the agency tariff table.

tasks.human_edge: Whether a site manager's volume story is credible, and how a flex-versus-own-staff frame will land with the people and the works council, is something the controller judges in the room. The copilot cannot run that conversation or start a works-council route.
tasks.pattern_why: The cycle is predictable: collect, tie to AFAS, question the drivers, challenge, lock. The controller stays the lead because the work is directing people and choosing a frame. An agent that chased site managers on its own would bypass that lead.

in_practice.trigger: The budget calendar opens, or a site's volume forecast moves far enough that the agency-labour line no longer matches the plan.
steps: Site submissions and AFAS year-to-date actuals are pulled into one pack per site, with own staff and agency labour on separate lines.
The copilot drafts questions on lines that break a driver, such as hours per shipment, the agency tariff, or overtime under the relevant CAO.
The controller holds the challenge meeting with the site manager and the FP&A analyst.
Any frame that changes the mix of own staff and flex is written so the Finance Director can see the works-council route before a promise is made.
The Finance Director locks the plan. The locked file is stored with the driver set.
in_practice.human_gate: A site pack is not the budget until the Finance Director locks it. A frame that changes staffing is not sent to the works council by the copilot.
data_needed: CAO wage and allowance structure for both CAOs
Prior forecast and the locked budget
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint budget folder, with the locked version, the driver set, the questions used and the meeting decision.

evidence.claim: Directing a budget across three sites is coordination and challenge. No reviewed product runs a Dutch site budget, with agency labour separated, on AFAS Profit.
Where the plan includes placing a surplus or drawing funds, cash allocation still needs a person's approval and a timestamped log.

risks: A fluent site pack can launder a flex assumption nobody defended in the meeting. The challenge questions have to be answered by a named manager.
A frame that shifts work from CAO staff to agencies can be a works-council matter. Treating the pack as finished skips that route.
If the FP&A driver file is wrong, faster consolidation spreads the wrong plan to three sites.
Peak agency tariffs that live only in a portal PDF will not tie to the flex line until the invoice arrives.
research_questions: How many Excel versions circulate in one budget round, and how many days does the consolidation take?
Do site managers see agency hours as a separate line today, and do they receive the pack before or after the lock?
Which budget changes in the last two years had to go to the works council, and who wrote the financial note?
How far off was last year's site flex forecast against the agency invoices that actually arrived?

tasks.short: Advise management on the financial choices in front of them.

today.trigger: A management meeting, a question from the Finance Director, or the works council asking for the figures.
steps: Collect the latest close, the cash position, days sales outstanding and the forecast gap.
Turn them into a note or a PowerPoint deck.
Decide what to recommend and what the figures do not support.
Present the advice and answer questions from management.
Write down what was decided.
drudgery: Reformatting the same tables the night before the meeting
Rebuilding an appendix from the nightly extract
Correcting slides that do not match the ledger
today.time_sinks: Producing the pack, and the rework when a figure in the slides does not match AFAS.

lenses.faster: Building the pack from a blank page disappears. Making the recommendation defensible, and the management meeting itself, still take about half a day per paper.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the management agenda is set or the Finance Director asks for a view on terms, the reserve, capex or flex. A sourced pack and two alternative recommendations are drafted. The gate is the controller signing the advice before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: The works council receives a short financial note in Dutch at its regular meetings, drawn from the same figures as the management pack, instead of a long paper mainly when the annual accounts are ready. Demand would grow if that note were cheap, because the council's right to financial information recurs through the year and the cost of a full pack is what limits it now.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting tables into slides. The controller keeps the choice of which objective to move, days to close, the forecast or days sales outstanding, and what not to promise.
lenses.options: Two policies, tighter customer payment terms or a higher cash reserve, ask management for different decisions and move days sales outstanding and the facility in opposite directions. A third draft that cuts the flex budget changes what the works council will need to hear. The draft that is sent is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The controller walks in with a sourced note and spends the meeting on the choice. They gain the right to put a recommendation on the agenda, and management keeps the decision. The job becomes more expert on how the company makes its result, and less on producing slides.
reach: The FP&A analyst's forecast-versus-actual commentary for the management pack, once the controller learns the volume and tariff bridges the analysts use.

tasks.human_edge: What to say when the numbers are ugly, what to leave out of a works-council note, and what management will treat as a promise are judgements the controller makes. A draft that reads well is not yet advice the business can trust. The controller signs it.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack can be assembled from the locked close and the treasury log, and a model can draft alternatives. The advice itself is the controller's, given in the room, so the person stays the lead. The steps of a paper are known in advance, which rules out an agent.

in_practice.trigger: The management meeting agenda is set, or the Finance Director asks for a policy view on payment terms, the reserve, capex or flex.
steps: A pack is assembled from the locked close, the treasury log and the forecast, with each figure pointing at an AFAS account or a SharePoint file.
The copilot drafts two recommendations, each with the effect on days to close, forecast accuracy, days sales outstanding and agency cost.
The controller rewrites the recommendation and removes anything the sources do not support.
If the works council will see the outcome, the controller edits a short Dutch note from the same figures and decides what stays in the management pack only.
Management decides. The note that was sent and the decision are stored together.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs the advice before it goes to management or the works council. The copilot does not send it.
data_needed: A list of figures cleared for the works council
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint management-papers folder, with the source for every figure, the draft, the signed version and the decision.

evidence.claim: On 160 US GAAP close tasks the leading result meets 61.8% of criteria and 58% of tasks are never fully solved. The published bottleneck is accounting judgement, not retrieval, which is the part a management paper still requires from the controller.
An estimate built in a personal model account, where prompt and output are not kept, cannot be rebuilt by an auditor. The same gap applies to a management paper.
The benchmarks behind these results are US GAAP. Dutch GAAP under BW 2 Titel 9, and the way a Dutch works council is informed, are not covered by them.

risks: Management treats a fluent draft as the recommendation and skips the controller's rewrite.
A works-council note that copies the management pack can disclose facility headroom or customer margins the board has not released.
US GAAP wording in a draft, for example on provisions or revenue, will misstate a Dutch pack.
Figures taken from the nightly Power BI extract instead of the locked close will not match what the Finance Director signed.
research_questions: Which decisions in the last four management meetings turned on a paper from the controller, and which were taken from a verbal update?
What financial information does the works council receive today, how often, and how many hours does it take?
Which figures in the management pack are too sensitive for a works-council note?
How often has management asked for advice between the budget and the next close?

tasks.short: Budget the insurance and benefit premiums and read the renewals.

today.trigger: An insurer renewal, a CAO or pension circular, the budget cycle, or a loss that moves a casualty premium.
steps: Collect the policies, the last invoices, the AFAS headcount and the broker's PDF.
Separate own staff from flex workers, and the transport CAO from the warehouse CAO.
Build the premium budget, including wage continuation during illness.
Discuss insure versus own risk with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist and the Finance Director.
Book the accrual once the invoice or the renewal is agreed.
drudgery: Retyping premium tables out of broker PDFs
Reconciling an insurer's headcount to AFAS and removing flex workers who should not be in the base
Finding last year's invoice when the summary does not match the ledger
today.time_sinks: Reading the renewal, and the hunt through last year's files when the broker's number and AFAS disagree.

lenses.faster: Retyping renewal PDFs, CAO circulars and last year's invoices into a comparison disappears as blank-page work. Checking every figure against the invoice, and agreeing the frame with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist, still takes the review and the meeting, most of a day at renewal.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a renewal, a CAO circular or an insurer invoice arrives. One pass turns those documents into a comparison against the budget. The gate is the controller and the Finance Director accepting the budget line and any own-risk choice.
lenses.ambitious: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist gets a costed note when a CAO change or a renewal moves the pension or absence-insurance cost, in time for the works council, instead of waiting for the annual budget. Demand would grow outside the budget cycle, because the specialist would ask at each renewal and CAO round if the comparison were quick to produce.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping premium tables. The controller keeps the renewal decision: insure the absence risk, carry more of it, or re-tender the fleet and cargo cover, and what that does to the result.
lenses.options: Three frames for absence cost, insure it, carry part of it, or carry the WGA risk ourselves, change the budget and the month in which sick pay hits cash. Those frames are different decisions for the Finance Director, not three wordings of one memo.
lenses.altitude: Renewal month becomes a one-page comparison and a meeting with the broker and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist. The controller gains the right to recommend the funding frame and to refuse an accrual the invoice does not support. The specialist keeps employee communication and the works-council conversation on the scheme itself. The controller becomes more expert on the cost of the two CAOs, and less of a transcriber.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first comparison of a renewal against the budget, once the controller learns the pension and industry-fund premiums in both CAOs and which files are illness records.

tasks.human_edge: The broker negotiation, the choice to carry an absence or WGA risk, and any file that touches a person's health or a Wet verbetering poortwachter case stay with people. The Compensation and Benefits Specialist keeps the scheme and the employee. The controller's edge is the cost and the cash timing, checked against the invoice.
tasks.pattern_why: A renewal, a circular and an invoice are messy documents, and one model call can turn them into a comparison a person can check against the source. The workflow after that is fixed: check, choose a frame, accrue. An agent is not required, and the calculation of a person's benefit is not this task.

in_practice.trigger: A renewal, a CAO or pension circular, or an insurer invoice arrives.
steps: The model reads the renewal, the circular and the last paid invoice, and drafts a one-page comparison: premium, headcount base, term, exclusion and the change versus budget.
The draft keeps flex workers out of the own-staff base, keeps the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO apart, and uses company totals only.
The controller checks every euro against the invoice or the policy and corrects the draft.
The controller and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist choose insure, partial own risk, or a changed deductible, and set the budget line.
An accrual above the Finance Director's threshold is posted in AFAS only after that approval.
in_practice.human_gate: No premium, own-risk choice or benefit-budget line is final until the controller accepts the figures and the Finance Director accepts a change above the threshold. Employee communication stays with Compensation and Benefits.
data_needed: Current policies and last paid invoices
AFAS headcount by CAO and site
Flex headcount kept off the insured base
Claims totals at policy level, with no individual claims
Budget line for benefits, absence and casualty
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint insurance folder with the source PDF, the draft, the corrected note and the approval. Individual claim files and illness records are not stored there and are not put in the prompt.

evidence.claim: Dutch employer cost here is pension, wage continuation and absence or WGA cover, plus fleet, property and cargo policies. It is not a US health plan or a US workers' compensation policy, so a US benefits workflow does not transfer.
No reviewed product summarises Dutch CAO premiums or insurer renewals into an AFAS budget line. A draft still has to be checked against the invoice by a person.
A cost estimate whose prompt and output sit in a personal account cannot be rebuilt later. A premium accrual needs the source PDF and the corrected note on file.

risks: Illness data and individual claims are special-category data under the AVG. Putting a Wet verbetering poortwachter file or a claim list into the prompt is the failure to avoid.
Flex workers insured through the agencies will be double-counted if the model adds them to the own-staff premium base.
Blending the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO produces a premium base neither fund will recognise.
A wrong summary of a CAO circular looks like a budget. Every euro has to trace to an invoice or a published rate.
Changing a benefit scheme can require works-council consent. A finished-looking cost note does not start that procedure.
Using the model to score individual employees or claims would move this into worker-related uses under the EU AI Act. The draft stays at policy and company level.
research_questions: Which policies does Noordhaven hold for absence, WGA, pension, fleet, property and cargo, and which of those does the controller budget rather than the Compensation and Benefits Specialist?
Are flex workers excluded from the insured headcount, and where is that exclusion written?
What share of renewal time is reading PDFs, and what share is the broker meeting?
Which benefit changes needed works-council consent last time, and did finance supply a cost note before that meeting?

tasks.short: Account for wage tax, pension and the other payroll withholdings.

today.trigger: Each AFAS payroll run, the wage-tax filing, a pension or industry-fund invoice, and month end.
steps: Take the payroll journal and the wage summary from the Payroll Specialist.
Check wage tax, pension and CAO-fund amounts against the totals AFAS produced.
Reconcile the journal to the general ledger and to the pension invoice.
Explain the difference, or ask payroll to correct the run before filing.
Support the wage-tax filing and post any correcting journal.
drudgery: Ticking the same wage, tax and pension totals every run
Rebuilding the bridge workbook from payroll journal to ledger to invoice
Splitting a difference that is only the timing of the pension invoice
today.time_sinks: Runs that do not tie, especially when shift allowances, a holiday-allowance payout or a correction hits, and any question about whether a flex worker was put on the own payroll by mistake.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the bridge from the payroll journal to the ledger, the wage-tax return and the pension invoice disappears on runs that tie. Reviewing a real break, and supporting the filing, still takes about an hour on a clean run and half a day when an allowance or the holiday-allowance payout does not tie.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when AFAS closes a payroll run or a pension invoice arrives. The model drafts the bridge and the flux line from totals only. The gate is a tie-out that blocks the journal, and the controller's approval before the filing is supported.
lenses.ambitious: Whether a difference is timing or a wrong CAO mapping is decided on each pay run, for both CAOs, instead of only when the month-end accrual looks odd. Demand would grow, because payroll would send the smaller shift-allowance breaks they now hold until the quarter.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking the same boxes by hand. The controller keeps the breaks that mean something: an allowance on the wrong ledger account, or agency staff posted onto the own payroll.
lenses.options: Two treatments of the same break, book it as timing against the pension invoice, or correct the pay run before the wage-tax filing, change the return and next month's flux. The controller chooses one before the Payroll Specialist files.
lenses.altitude: Pay week starts from a bridge that is either clean or a short list. The controller gains the right to stop support for the filing when the wage total, the ledger and the return do not agree, and to send the break back to payroll. The Payroll Specialist keeps the employee-level calculation. The controller becomes more expert on the payroll-to-ledger map, and less of a re-ticker.
reach: The accountant's posting of the standard payroll journal once the tie-out is clean, once the controller learns the AFAS payroll-to-ledger map and can read a break on either CAO.

tasks.human_edge: The controller decides whether a break is a real under-withholding that must be corrected before the Belastingdienst filing. Attachments of earnings and any individual sick-pay marker stay with payroll and out of the model. The person who signs the wage-tax return still signs it.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already computes the statutory withholdings with wage-tax tables and the CAO. The messy remainder is the bridge: why the journal, the ledger, the wage-tax return and the pension invoice differ. One draft plus a deterministic tie-out is enough. A model must not recompute an employee's deduction.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS closes a payroll run, or a pension or industry-fund invoice arrives.
steps: Employee-level wage tax, pension, CAO funds and other withholdings stay in AFAS, which applies the statutory tables and the CAO.
Only totals by CAO and site are passed across, with no attachment-of-earnings file and no illness codes.
The model drafts the bridge between the payroll journal, the general ledger, the wage-tax return and the pension creditor, and a flux line for any break.
A query blocks posting while the wage total, the ledger and the return disagree.
The controller approves a clean bridge, or sends the break back to the Payroll Specialist before the filing is supported.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves the bridge journal each run. The person who signs the loonheffingen return signs it. The model never changes an employee's withholding.
data_needed: Payroll journal totals by CAO and site
A check that flex workers are not on this payroll
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal trail and a SharePoint payroll-bridge folder with the totals, the draft, the tie-out result and the approver. Not the payslips, and not a personal model account.

evidence.claim: The documented control pattern is that the model drafts and the tie-out decides: nothing posts until bank, accounts receivable and accounts payable tie to zero. Applied here, the payroll journal does not post until it ties to the wage total and the return.

AFAS payroll already calculates Dutch wage tax and employee withholdings. The controller's remaining work is the bridge to the ledger, the return and the pension creditor, not a second calculation of the tables.
A payroll bridge that exists only in a personal model account cannot be rebuilt for the wage-tax filing or the auditor.

risks: A model that 'corrects' a statutory withholding will create a filing error. It may draft the journal only.
Flex workers paid by the agencies, under inlenersbeloning, are not this payroll. Including them double-counts cost that already sits in accounts payable.
The two CAOs do not share one pension or fund base. A single bridge will hide a wrong mapping.
Attachments of earnings and sick-pay markers are employee data under the AVG. They do not belong in the prompt. A tool that starts reading employee-level payroll can be a works-council matter.
Holiday-allowance payout months will break a bridge that assumes a normal run. Those months need their own line in the test.
research_questions: Who signs the loonheffingen return, and how many corrections were filed in the last year?
What share of pay runs already tie to the general ledger and the pension invoice with no manual journal?
Have agency workers appeared on the AFAS payroll in the last year, even for one run?
Which payroll files contain attachments of earnings or sick-pay markers, and who is allowed to see them?

tasks.short: Direct the monthly statements, the forecast and the filings.

today.trigger: Month end, the forecast cycle, year end, or a VAT or Chamber of Commerce deadline.
steps: Direct the accountants to close the sub-ledgers and prepare the accrual schedules.
Review the trial balance, the three sites and the flux against last month and the forecast.
Decide the judgements: unbilled agency hours, holiday allowance, claims, depreciation and provisions.
Direct the statement pack, the forecast bridge and the regulatory returns.
Walk the Finance Director and, at year end, the auditor through those judgements.
drudgery: Rewriting flux comments that name a variance and give no cause
Chasing the same rent, depreciation and holiday-allowance schedules every month
Checking that the pack, the Power BI extract and the ledger still agree
today.time_sinks: The days between a closed sub-ledger and a pack the Finance Director will sign, above all the agency accrual and any line that fails a tie-out.

lenses.faster: First drafts of the standard accruals, the reclasses and the flux commentary disappear. Review of every material judgement, the tie-out, the forecast bridge and the returns AFAS does not file still takes about three fifths of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the sub-ledgers are closed for the period. The model drafts the handbook accruals and the flux by site, and a tie-out runs first. The gate is the controller approving each proposed journal before it posts, and signing the pack.
lenses.ambitious: A forecast the site managers can use to change flex orders is refreshed when volume or agency hours move, while the month is still open, instead of arriving only with the closed pack. Demand would grow in volatile weeks, because a site would ask for that refresh when flex hours jump and today they wait while the close is still being produced.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss flux sentences that say a cost is higher and stop there. The controller keeps the accruals that are actually in doubt, the unbilled agency hours, a cargo claim, the holiday-allowance reserve, and the conversation with the auditor.
lenses.options: Two treatments of unbilled agency hours, accrue at the contracted rate or accrue only the hours the site has confirmed, change the month's result and the forecast. A third treatment of a cargo claim, book a provision or disclose it as contingent, changes what the auditor is asked to accept. The treatment is the decision.
lenses.altitude: Close week becomes a drafted pack, a short list of judgements and a forecast conversation with the Finance Director. The controller gains the right to set the materiality line and the accrual methods the draft must follow, and to reject a pack that fails the tie-out. The accountants keep the sub-ledger detail. The job becomes more expert on judgement and method, and less on assembling statements.
reach: The accountant's first draft of the monthly flux and the standard accrual journals for rent, depreciation and holiday allowance, once the controller can separate a voorziening from a contingent liability under BW 2 Titel 9 and post an approved journal in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: The controller decides what is a voorziening, whether the agency accrual is complete, what the auditor will accept, and what the forecast should admit it does not know. A lab result on simple month-end cases did not measure that judgement, the questions to the sites, or the conversation with the auditor. Signing the statements and the VAT return stays with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Standard accruals and flux commentary are one draft from a fixed handbook, inside a close that follows the same order every month. A deterministic tie-out of bank, receivables, payables and payroll decides whether anything can post. The open judgements are a short list for the controller, not a reason to let an agent post.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS sub-ledgers for the period are closed, or working day one of the close calendar, whichever the controller has set.
steps: Queries confirm that bank, receivables and payables tie to the general ledger, and that the payroll journal ties to the wage totals. A failed tie stops the draft.
The model drafts accrual and reclass journals from the handbook: unbilled agency hours, rent, depreciation, holiday allowance and pension. It drafts flux commentary by site from the ledger movements.
Amounts above the materiality line, and any voorziening or contingent-liability choice, are listed separately with the source balance.
The controller accepts, adjusts or rejects each proposed journal. Approved journals are posted by an accountant in AFAS.

The pack, statements, commentary and the forecast bridge, is written to SharePoint with the handbook version. The VAT return, and the SBR filing if Noordhaven is in the large-company class, are prepared by a person outside this draft.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing posts until the tie-out is clean and the controller has approved the journal. The controller signs the pack. The model cannot override a failed tie-out.
data_needed: Agency hours confirmed but not yet invoiced
CAO rates used for holiday allowance and pension
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close folder and the AFAS journal audit trail, with the handbook version, the prompt, the output, the tie-out result and the approver's time. Not a personal model account.

evidence.claim: Trintech's accruals agent generates and rolls forward accruals, flags outliers, and then requires Review & Approve and Retain for Audit.

SAP's accruals agent, in restricted availability, prepares journals for an accountant to accept, adjust or reject. Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and leaves review with the team. None of these agents runs on AFAS Profit.
On 160 US GAAP close tasks the leading result meets 61.8% of criteria and 58% of tasks are never fully solved. The bottleneck reported on that benchmark is accounting judgement, not retrieval.
In a vendor-run lab, twelve licensed CPAs averaged about 37% on four simple month-end scenarios. The study did not measure client communication, asking the right questions, or building tacit context.
Choi and Xie found accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms, while 62% of 277 surveyed accountants worried about errors.
Nothing should post until bank, accounts receivable and accounts payable tie to zero. The draft does not get a vote where the tie fails.
AFAS cannot produce the SBR filing that large companies must send to the KVK from financial year 2025.
These close benchmarks are US GAAP. Dutch GAAP under BW 2 Titel 9, the statutory audit and the VAT return are untested by them.

risks: If the close waits on agency invoices and warehouse counts, a faster draft does not shorten days to close.
A fluent flux comment can hide a forecast the sites still do not trust. Forecast accuracy is a separate test from a finished pack.
US GAAP habits in a draft, especially on provisions and presentation, will not survive a Dutch audit under BW 2 Titel 9.
Posting from the nightly Power BI extract, rather than the tie-out on AFAS, will not match the ledger the auditor sees.
A pack whose prompt lives in a personal account cannot be reperformed. The handbook version and the output have to sit in the close folder.
Holiday allowance and pension accrued on a headcount that includes flex workers overstates the liability. Flex cost belongs with the agency accrual.
The VAT return and, for a large company, the SBR filing are outside the evidence. Leaving them in the draft would overclaim what the model can file.
research_questions: In the last six closes, where did the days go: waiting for agency invoices and site counts, tying the sub-ledgers, drafting accruals, or the judgement discussion?
What share of month-end journals repeat a method a handbook can name, and what share are one-off judgements?
Will the statutory auditor rely on a drafted accrual when the handbook, the prompt and the approver are on file, or reperform every material line?
Is Noordhaven in the large-company size class for SBR, and who files the KVK accounts and the VAT return today?

role.altitude: The controller's week moves from assembling the cash position, the payment checks and the close pack to judging the short list those drafts cannot settle, and to telling the Finance Director and the sites what the figures mean while there is still time to act. Decision rights that grow are the accrual methods, the materiality line, the reserve floor and the right to stop a batch, a filing or a pack that fails its tie-out. The Finance Director still locks the budget, places the cash and sits on the management team. The job becomes more expert, because the hours that remain are the judgements, the audit and the forecast the business is asked to trust.
reach: The accountant's first draft of monthly flux and the standard accruals for rent, depreciation and holiday allowance, once the controller can post an approved journal in AFAS and separate a voorziening from a contingent liability under BW 2 Titel 9.
The bookkeeper's work on duplicate-invoice stops, IBAN changes and bank lines the AFAS rules do not match, once the controller knows the agency rate cards and the bank-match screen.
The FP&A analyst's assembly of the 13-week cash view and the site forecast pack, once the controller knows the volume, tariff and agency-hour drivers for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first cost comparison of an insurer renewal, once the controller knows both CAOs' pension and fund premiums and keeps illness files out of the work.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 45% of the role. Leading the accountants and bookkeepers, the Rabobank mandate, the auditor and the works council do not shrink the way a tie-out does. One controller cannot take the jobs of two accountants, three bookkeepers and two FP&A analysts. Dutch GAAP judgements, the VAT return and an SBR filing that AFAS does not produce for large companies set a floor under year-end hours. In the peak, 150 to 300 flex workers show up as agency invoices the rules will keep returning, and those exceptions stay.
skills_to_grow: An accrual handbook the auditor can reperform from AFAS and SharePoint, including materiality and the difference between a voorziening and a contingent liability under BW 2 Titel 9.
AFAS payment mandates, bank matching on CAMT.053, and the payroll-to-ledger map, so a rule is changed once instead of checked by hand.
The Rabobank facility, SEPA batch approval and a 13-week cash view that counts unbilled agency hours.
Enough of both CAOs, wage tax and the pension invoices to read a break, and to keep flex workers off the own payroll and the insured headcount.
What the works council is entitled to see, and which employee data, illness and attachments of earnings, never goes into a prompt.
The SBR path to the KVK for a company in the large size class, because AFAS will not produce that filing.
role.ambitious_version: The controller runs a close the Finance Director can sign in fewer days, and in the same cycle produces a forecast each site manager can use to change flex orders while the month is still open, plus a short financial note the works council can read. A weekly place-or-draw recommendation is on the Finance Director's desk in peak weeks, and a person still signs every movement at Rabobank. The controller is willing to be judged on days to close, forecast accuracy and audit adjustments.
